rationale: Base rates first: cumulative AI-related economic damages (largely AI-enabled fraud, deepfake scams, and AI-assisted cyber operations) already run at ~$1-4B/yr and rising, so the $1B and $10B rungs of the AI and cyber ladders are likely-to-near-certain over 1-5 year horizons; the death-based and >$100B rungs require qualitatively new events (AI-enabled critical-infrastructure attacks, engineered pandemics, large loss-of-control incidents) and are anchored to low historical base rates (no human-caused epidemic >100 deaths since 1979 Sverdlovsk; largest cyber event, NotPetya, ~$10B) adjusted upward for rapidly growing capability (autonomous agent attacks documented since Nov 2025, falling biosecurity screening barriers). Ladders decay roughly 3-5x per severity decade near-term, flattening at long horizons where engineered-pandemic and loss-of-control tails dominate; cross-cutting estimates sit between XPT superforecaster (~9%/2.1%) and domain-expert (~20%/12%) figures for 10%-mortality catastrophes by 2100. Policy conditions are modeled as multipliers holding world riskiness fixed: status quo (no further policy) modestly raises risk vs. the unconditional path (~1.05-1.3x, larger at tails/long horizons); P1 preemption slightly raises risk (~1.0-1.1x); P2a (US-only slowdown) gives small reductions since China and open-weight models continue; P3a and P4 give moderate reductions (~10-20% at tails) via deployment gating and internalized liability incentives for US developers; P2b and P3b (US-China binding measures) cut mid-century tail risks ~25-35%; the P5 bundle is strongest (~40-55% tail reduction by 2050, attenuating by 2100 since capabilities eventually arrive and the policies lapse in 2050). Effects are minimal at 6-12 months (implementation lag, harms driven by already-deployed systems) and compressed for near-saturated low rungs driven by commodity AI misuse. Misalignment and bio ladders get the largest policy sensitivity (frontier-development-gated risks); low-rung cyber/fraud the least.

rationale: Base rates first: cumulative AI-related economic damages (largely AI-enabled fraud, deepfake scams, and AI-assisted cyber operations) already run at ~$1-4B/yr and rising, so the $1B and $10B rungs of the AI and cyber ladders are likely-to-near-certain over 1-5 year horizons; the death-based and >$100B rungs require qualitatively new events (AI-enabled critical-infrastructure attacks, engineered pandemics, large loss-of-control incidents) and are anchored to low historical base rates (no human-caused epidemic >100 deaths since 1979 Sverdlovsk; largest cyber event, NotPetya, ~$10B) adjusted upward for rapidly growing capability (autonomous agent attacks documented since Nov 2025, falling biosecurity screening barriers). Ladders decay roughly 3-5x per severity decade near-term, flattening at long horizons where engineered-pandemic and loss-of-control tails dominate; cross-cutting estimates sit between XPT superforecaster (~9%/2.1%) and domain-expert (~20%/12%) figures for 10%-mortality catastrophes by 2100. Policy conditions are modeled as multipliers holding world riskiness fixed: status quo (no further policy) modestly raises risk vs. the unconditional path (~1.05-1.3x, larger at tails/long horizons); P1 preemption slightly raises risk (~1.0-1.1x); P2a (US-only slowdown) gives small reductions since China and open-weight models continue; P3a and P4 give moderate reductions (~10-20% at tails) via deployment gating and internalized liability incentives for US developers; P2b and P3b (US-China binding measures) cut mid-century tail risks ~25-35%; the P5 bundle is strongest (~40-55% tail reduction by 2050, attenuating by 2100 since capabilities eventually arrive and the policies lapse in 2050). Effects are minimal at 6-12 months (implementation lag, harms driven by already-deployed systems) and compressed for near-saturated low rungs driven by commodity AI misuse. Misalignment and bio ladders get the largest policy sensitivity (frontier-development-gated risks); low-rung cyber/fraud the least.
key_sources: FBI IC3 2025 Internet Crime Report (~$893M AI-related crime losses; $20.9B total)
Surfshark/Resemble deepfake fraud loss tracking ($2.2-3.7B cumulative, 89% in 2025-H1 2026)
Deloitte Center for Financial Services genAI fraud projection ($40B/yr US by 2027)
Anthropic Nov 2025 disclosure of first largely autonomous AI-orchestrated cyber-espionage campaign
METR Frontier Risk Report (May 2026)
Forecasting Research Institute XPT (catastrophe/extinction estimates)
Metaculus Q1493 (~35% population decline >10% by 2100) and Ragnarok series
Frontier Model Forum biosafety thresholds; Anthropic RSP updates 2026
FRI 'Forecasting LLM-enabled biorisk' report
